title: fracture-batch-runloop-into-lightweight-executors-and-kv-sampler
creator: Aisha Kaur
description: Summary: This ticket refactors the monolithic continuous batch runloop into several lightweight executor components and introduces a separate 'KV sampler' service that asynchronously primes and scores KV cache candidates. Motivation: The current runloop handles batching, admission, prefetch priming, and KV cache coordination in a single event strand which has accumulated conditional complexity and causes observable stalls during heavy churn (seen in production spikes on 2026-01-26). The monolith increases tail latency and makes targeted perf fixes risky. Goals: 1) Break the runloop into three cooperating executors (ingress coordinator, batch executor, and lifecycle steward) to reduce contention and make CPU/memory ownership explicit. 2) Extract prefetch/priming logic into a KV sampler that runs with looser SLOs and maintains a priority scoring queue (decoupled from the hot path). 3) Keep backwards-compatible RPC/handshake contracts so hosted API and dedicated deployments see no behavior change. 4) Reduce median and p95 generation latency under churn by 10-20% and CPU jitter by 25%. Scope: - Move admission token bucket and initial enqueue into the ingress coordinator. - Batch formation, slot allocation, and GPU dispatch remain in batch executor but with a thinner state machine. - Lifecycle steward handles slot reclamation, heartbeat, and graceful drain. - KV sampler manages async prefetch, backoff, sample scoring, and exposes metrics for primed keys. - Introduce instrumentation spans for new executor boundaries and end-to-end latency tracing. Design notes: - Communication between executors via lock-free queues and well-defined message contracts to avoid introducing global locks. - KV sampler uses a bounded in-memory priority queue and supports pluggable scoring heuristics (LRU-weighted hit-probability + recent-access boost). - Fallback flow: if sampler cannot respond, ingress coordinator downgrades to opportunistic prefetch in the batch executor to preserve correctness. - Backwards compatibility: RPC between request path and cache remains unchanged; internal scheduling messages are versioned. Trade-offs: - Slightly increased code surface area and more moving parts for debugging, but easier to reason about performance hotspots and safer incremental rollout. - Potential for transient duplicates in prefetch; sampler will deduplicate and coalesce requests. Rollout plan: 1) Feature-flagged implementation behind runtime-preexecutor gate. 2) Canary in a small fleet (10% traffic) with synthetic workload and real traffic mirroring. 3) Monitor latency, CPU, KV sampler hit-rate, and error budgets for 48 hours. 4) Gradual ramp to 50% then 100% if metrics stable. Metrics to track: - end_to_end_p50/p95_generation_ms (before vs after) - cpu_jitter_stddev (per-host, 1m window) - kv_prefetch_hit_rate and primed_keys_per_sec - batch_fill_ratio and average_batch_size - eviction_pressure and sampler_queue_latency Stability and testing: - Unit tests for message contracts, sampler scoring, and dedup behavior. - Integration tests in staging that replay production traces and verify ordering guarantees and no-loss semantics. - Load test to quantify tail-latency improvements and confirm no memory blowups under sustained high cardinality workloads. Migration and cleanups: - Phase 1: introduce executors + sampler behind flag. - Phase 2: switch default for new clusters and run for two weeks. - Phase 3: remove legacy runloop code paths and old metrics. Follow-ups: - Add ML-derived sampler heuristic (future ticket) - Surface sampler insights into Console (observability) - Explore moving sampler to dedicated thread pool for multi-tenant isolation Links: Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SERV/Fracture+Runloop+Design GitHub PR (WIP): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/7321 Production incident notes (2026-01-26): https://go.redwood.ai/incidents/2026-01-prefetch-stall
acceptance_criteria: Monolithic runloop code path is split such that no single executor holds admission, batching, and lifecycle responsibilities
KV sampler exists as a distinct module with documented scoring interface and has unit + integration tests
Canary rollout demonstrates >=10% median latency reduction and no increase in error rate for 48h on mirrored traffic
All RPC/handshake contracts remain backward compatible; no client changes required
New executor-level telemetry is emitted and dashboards created in Console for monitoring
